newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks firm, techs lead way.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks firm, techs lead way.

text.p: Stocks rose Friday as a resurgent technology sector re-assumed leadership of the bull market for the first time in weeks.

At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average rose 39.88 points to 6,458.35. In the broader market, advances outpaced declines by a margin of about 13 to eight on heavy volume of more than 306 million shares.
The technology-laden Nasdaq composite index gained 13.95 to 1,272.03, boosted by a sharp rally in semiconductor equipment companies.

"The strength seems to be tied to the techs and that would be a good thing," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities. "We're at a point now where we need to show major firepower to keep the rally going and the techs could provide that leadership."

Among the Dow components, International Business Machines Corp. remained the standout, climbing 2-3/4 to 156-7/8. The broad rally also pulled in a number of names that had failed to participate in the post-Election Day gains.

Semiconductor equipment maker Applied Materials Inc. was the clearest example, surging 7 to 39, despite reporting fourth-quarter earnings late Thursday that were about half the levels posted a year ago.
The company, however, told analysts during a conference call it did not expect the current cyclical downturn it faced would be as severe as those in the past.
The disclosure prompted a flurry of upgrades by Wall Street firms, with some raising ratings on Applied Materials' competitors as well.
Among other companies in the sector, KLA Instruments Corp. jumped 4-3/4 to 38, Tencor Instruments gained 4-1/4 to 25-1/2 and Lam Research Corp. rose 4-7/8 to 34-3/8.
Analysts said the rally came at a key time for the market, which lately has relied on the Dow for its steam.

"It would not be surprising to see some profit-taking in the big stocks," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "We're in a rotational market and we're at a point now where fund managers are ferreting through the list of stocks that have been beaten down since July."

Among individual issues, cosmetic company Nu Skin Asia Pacific Inc. bounded higher in its New York Stock Exchange debut. Shares jumped 6-1/2 to 29-1/2 on heavy volume in the first trading after Nu Skin's initial public offering.
Alrenco Inc. tumbled eight points to 11-1/2 after the company warned of weak fourth-quarter earnings.
Westell Technologies Inc., which warned its third-quarter results would fall short of expectations, slid 4-1/2 to 23-1/2. The shares were downgraded to neutral from buy by Cowen & Co.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 4.55 points to 747.30. The American Stock Exchange Composite climbed 2.31 points to 590.07.
